big: An AIF earns a profit. Investors get their preferred return first, say 10% a year. Only then does the manager take carry, often around 20% of further profits. Layers of fees and special tax treatment make AIFs different.

lines: Who pays tax in an AIF?

For Category I and II, income is generally taxed in the investor's hands, not the fund's. That is pass-through. The manager earns carry only after investors receive the preferred return. Most AIFs are trusts run by an investment manager. Always confirm tax with a CA.

rows: a trust, run by an investment manager
note: Tax treatment depends on structure and the Income Tax Act. Ask a CA.
